description: Sou o Kelson, técnico em eletrónica e automação industrial (Angola), com experiência em ESP32, Arduino, Raspberry Pi e instrumentação. Vamos criar um sistema vestível que monitoriza a saúde de astronautas e alerta sobre fadiga e anomalias. Procuro: eletrónica embarcada, telecomunicações/IoT, programação Python e dados, interface/painel e comunicação (pitch e vídeo).
summary: Astra MED Link is health-monitoring software for astronauts on long-duration missions. Instead of adding new hardware sensors, it provides an on-board intelligence layer that unifies data from existing equipment, learns each astronaut's personal baseline, and detects acute cardiovascular stress and cumulative fatigue locally without internet. A local AI assistant (Astra MED) explains alerts, suggests actions via voice and text, and takes over guidance when Earth cannot answer in time. The system simulates communication delays and outages, sending only critical summaries back to Earth. It directly supports astronaut autonomy, addressing a key gap on deep-space missions.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? Astra MED Link is an on-board health intelligence software designed for astronauts on long-space missions. It operates offline and locally on board, functioning as an autonomous medical support system when communication with Earth is delayed or disrupted. It ingests telemetry data from medical equipment using a common format, runs a baseline engine to detect mathematical deviations from each astronaut's personal baseline, and utilizes a local AI system to explain conditions, provide advice, and guide the crew locally if Earth cannot answer in time. During communication outages, it buffers data and sends summaries once a connection is re-established

  • What benefits does it have?
    • Autonomous Reliability: Enables local triage and real-time guidance offline during communication delays or blackouts.
    • Personalized Health Tracking: Treats each astronaut as their own "normal" rather than relying on generic population thresholds.
    • Optimized Bandwidth: Manages adaptive telemetry by buffering data during outages and transmitting only what matters to flight surgeons on Earth.
    • Interoperability: Accepts data from any medical device that communicates via a common format.
  • What is the intended impact of the project? The primary impact is ensuring safer autonomy for space crews operating far from Earth by reducing reliance on ground-based decision-making during critical moments. It aims to prevent dangerous treatment delays, lower the cognitive load on astronauts, and provide reliable on-board medical triage when every second counts.
    • AI and Models: Gemma 3, Claude (used during development), Kokoro/Piper, and Vosk.
    • Hardware & Data Modeling: Modeled using variables and alert categories derived from NASA LSAH (Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health) documentation.
    • Testing: Supported by 98 passing automated tests. (Note: The current demo relies on simulated data and incorporates no proprietary NASA datasets yet).
  • How is your project creative? Rather than treating space health monitoring as merely adding more physical sensors, Astra MED Link focuses on the software intelligence layer. It bridges the gap between raw biometric signals and actionable crew decisions by combining localized mathematical baseline tracking with conversational AI (voice and chat interfaces) specifically adapted for deep-space communication constraints.
    • Communication Constraints: Severe latency and complete signal loss windows between deep space and Earth.
    • Data Privacy & Personalization: The necessity of individualized health baselines ("each astronaut is their own normal") over fixed statistical averages.
    • Safety & Compliance: Built-in safeguards recognizing that the system provides decision support and local triage rather than replacing professional medical oversight (not an official medical device)
projectRefs: NASA Lifetime Surveillance of Astronaut Health (LSAH)
